cards.text: Paul is wrapping up his letter to the church in Thessalonica, and he just told them the Day of the Lord will come like a thief in the night. So, he says, encourage and build one another up. Now, at the very end, he's got a LIST, friend, and every line on it is short and every job on it is BIG.

cards.question: Paul opens his final instructions with a request. Who does he ask the brothers to acknowledge?

answers.text: Those who work hard and care for them
Those who have believed the longest
Those who give the most to the church

cards.text: Paul says, "In love, hold them in highest regard because of their work. Live in peace with one another." That last line takes three seconds to read and a LIFETIME to do, friend.

cards.question: Paul urges the brothers to admonish the unruly, ___ the fainthearted and ___ the weak.
Paul tells the brothers to be patient with each other but not with outsiders.

cards.text: Now the hardest one on the list. Somebody does you wrong, and your thumbs are ALREADY typing the reply in the group chat.

cards.question: When somebody in the church does wrong, what does Paul tell the brothers to make sure of?

answers.text: That no one repays evil for evil
That the leaders settle it quickly

cards.text: Instead, Paul says, "Always pursue what is good for one another and for all people." Then he goes rapid-fire, short commands with NO exceptions, like a coach yelling from the sideline with two minutes on the clock.

cards.question: Paul's rapid-fire list opens with two short commands about joy and prayer. Which two?

answers.text: Rejoice at all times and pray without ceasing
Rejoice on good days and pray every morning
Rejoice in private and pray in public

cards.question: Paul says giving thanks in every circumstance is God's will for the brothers in Christ Jesus.

cards.text: Paul says not to extinguish the Spirit and not to treat prophecies with contempt. Friend, you don't toss the WHOLE batch over one weird-looking cookie.

cards.question: Paul tells the brothers not to treat prophecies with contempt. What does he say to do instead?
After testing everything, Paul says to hold fast to what is good but to avoid only the worst kinds of evil.

cards.text: Then Paul's instructions turn into a prayer: may the God of peace Himself sanctify them completely, spirit, soul and body. Not a touch-up, friend, the WHOLE thing, and trust me, I know a little something about getting made new.

cards.question: Paul prays that their entire spirit, soul and body will be kept blameless at the ___ of our Lord Jesus Christ.
Paul says someone is faithful and will make all of this happen for the brothers. Who?

cards.text: Then Paul says, "Brothers, pray for us as well." He also tells them to greet all the brothers with a holy kiss, and if I tried that, friend, all you'd get is a face full of MUSTACHE.

cards.question: Paul charges the brothers before the Lord to have this letter read to all the brothers.

cards.text: And Paul signs off: "The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you." Short, sweet and sealed, baker, just like a cookie box ready to go.

findings.problem: Paul appears here for the first time but is never introduced. The card says only that he is wrapping up 'his letter.' The card also states who wrote the letter and who it went to, but cites only 5:2-11. That fact comes from 1 Thessalonians 1:1, which lists Paul, Silvanus and Timothy as the senders.

rule.text: **New people.** The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: The card states that Paul wrote this letter to the church in Thessalonica (1 Thessalonians 1:1), but that verse isn't in the card's citation.

rule.text: **References.** Every Bible fact he states carries its reference.

findings.problem: The right words 'encourage' and 'help' mean nearly the same thing and can be swapped. A baker who puts 'help the fainthearted' and 'encourage the weak' gets marked wrong, but could argue they're right. The card also asks the baker to guess the wording of v14, which hasn't been shown.

rule.text: **No near-matches.** A wrong answer never means the same as the right answer, or close to it. If a baker could argue it's right, replace it.

findings.problem: The card cites v15 but tells nothing from it. It is only a setup joke about wanting to reply in a group chat, with no part of the passage on the card.

rule.text: Every story card tells part of the passage. Jokes ride along on those cards.

findings.problem: The question says 'When somebody in the church does wrong.' Verse 15 doesn't limit the command to wrongs done inside the church. It says 'no one repays evil for evil' and goes on to say 'for one another and for all people.' The question narrows what the text leaves open.

rule.text: **Leave open what the text leaves open:** who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: The setup says the commands that follow come 'with NO exceptions.' That rules out the wrong answers on later cards: card 9's 'on good days' and 'every morning,' card 10's 'every circumstance' (true), and card 13's 'avoid only the worst kinds of evil' (false).

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The card ties 'spirit, soul and body' to 'sanctify them completely.' In v23, 'entire spirit, soul, and body' goes with being 'kept blameless at the coming,' in a separate clause. Merging the two clauses changes how the text connects them.

rule.text: **Leave open what the text leaves open:** who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: The question says the One who calls them 'will make all of this happen.' Verse 24 says only 'He will do it.' 'All of this' widens the claim to the whole list of instructions, and the text doesn't say that.

rule.text: **Don't stretch the text.** Exaggerate only in his own jokes.
